title: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos — Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition, 5.8 Evaluating point forecast accuracy
use: Further study of forecast versus fitted errors, MAE/RMSE units and percentage-denominator limitations. The chapter develops original examples and an explicit separate validation role.
verification: Retrieved author-hosted chapter; inspected training/test, error definitions, scale-dependent and percentage error sections. Source illustrative datasets and code are not reproduced. Its approximate sample split size is not adopted as a universal rule; empirical claims in its examples are not claimed as independently verified.

title: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos — Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition, 5.10 Time series cross-validation
use: Further study of rolling origins and horizon-specific forecast evaluation. The original lab adds explicit releases, candidate selection and fixed-origin versus updating protocols.
verification: Retrieved author-hosted chapter and inspected temporal order and repeated-origin/horizon discussion. Did not reproduce its Google data/results, figures or R examples. No universal claim that residual error must be below realized forecast error or horizons must worsen every case is adopted.

title: scikit-learn developers — Common pitfalls: Data leakage
use: Training-only learning of preprocessing transformations and applying them consistently on held-out data. Principle is used in an original small stdlib teaching case, without a scikit-learn dependency.
verification: Retrieved official documentation and inspected sections12.1–12.2 on preprocessing, leakage and per-split feature selection. Source library examples are not copied. Live documentation is not a claim about an exact historical point release; leakage is defined relative to the declared task, including explicitly different transductive tasks.

title: Gavin C. Cawley and Nicola L. C. Talbot (2010), On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
use: Original research route on optimizing noisy model-selection criteria and evaluation bias. Chapter supplies its own finite two-candidate example and expectation inequality.
verification: Retrieved JMLR original paper landing page and inspected abstract and bibliographic record, volume11 pages2079–2107. Full article calculations are not claimed as independently checked; citation supports the topic/further-study route, not the chapter original numerical demonstration.
